Title: ANIMATION MODE: Garment Animation Making
Content: Objective Tips for creating stable and realistic garment animation for multi-layered garments. Operation Optimize 3D Garment for Animation The heavier the garment, the slower and harder it records. Follow the steps below to make it lighter. For a multi-layered garment, increase particle distance to 20mm for inner layers that are not as visible as outer layers. Delete invisible and any other unnecessary layers. Outer layers: Set the particle distance to 10mm for parts that does not require higher level of expression of wrinkles. Set the particle distance to 5mm for parts that require higher level of expression of wrinkles. If there is large quantity of layers set to 5mm, set all of them to 7mm. Fix Garment If garment is not fixed to avatar while recording the animation, the garment moves drastically around the avatar due to collision. Certain parts of the garment need to be fixed to the avatar or itself to create more realistic recording. Use functions such as 'Avatar Tape' or 'Tack on Avatar' to attach shoulder and sides of the garment. Use 'Tack' function for overlapped layers or any parts that may dangle. Increase Transition Animation Time Increase the transition animation time for heavier garments. In the animation dialogue, enter 5FPS to stabilize the simulation. This makes the avatar movement slower which helps to minimize the collision between the garments. Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for the First Recording Setting Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' minimizes the collision between the avatar and garments. To save time, the simulation quality can be set to 'Normal' for the middle part of the recording as the avatar and garments tend to collide more in the beginning and end. Make sure the simulation to set the quality back on 'Complete' for the end of the Transition Animation. Reevaluate Draping of the Garment after the Recording As the avatar moves, some parts of the garment may collide. When the simulation is off, the 3D garment may appear fine, however there is possibility of unnoticeable collision which may destabilize rest of the recording. Return to Simulation Mode. Note: From ver2.5.0, it is possible to simulate by pressing the Simulation button without recording it. Active simulation and make sure the entire garment simulation is stable. If any parts of the garment is unstable, readjust the layers by using the Select/Move tool. Once the simulation has been stabilized, go back to the Animation Mode. Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' when Recording the Actual Garment Animation Make sure to set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for final recordings of Garment Animation as the 'Complete' and the 'Normal' give clearly different results in expressing reality.

Title: There is another similar software called CLO, what is the difference?
Content: We have two different products called Marvelous Designer and CLO that have been specifically designed for the entertainment and fashion industries, respectively. While similar, CLO is equipped with additional features that are essential to fashion designers including avatar size adjustability and support for DXF-AAMA (drawing) files. On the other hand, Marvelous Designer including UV editor, sculpt mode Other features unique to CLO are: The ability to measure the avatar as a tailor would, tech pack (specifications) feature, diverse stitching visuals, and advanced CAD features. To learn more about CLO, please visit www.clo3d.com

Title: Freeze/Unfreeze
Content: Objective Use this function to fasten Patterns like solid objects. For example, deactivated Patterns do not collide during Simulation however, frozen Patterns do. Therefore it is better to use it for draping multiple layered Garments. For instance, draping and freezing inner Garments first, then draping outerwear simultaneously, solves the occasional instabilities. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Freeze / Unfreeze 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Freeze / Unfreeze Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Freeze / Unfreeze 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Freeze / Unfreeze The selected Pattern is now being frozen/unfrozen. Title: Animation Guide
Content: Animation Workflow Import an Avatar Import an Alembic or FBX avatar with animation(e.g., Mixamo, Daz, User own created) into Marvelous Designer. Create a garment for the avatar in Marvelous Designer Create fabric items that fit on the imported avatar. Simulation Retopology Create quad meshes with the Topology tool if needed. When using 'Remeshing,' some unwanted triangle meshes might be created. If you want all the surfaces to be quad meshes, please use the 'Patch Topology' or 'Create Topology' instead. Recording It is recommended to set the simulation quality as 'Animation(Stable)' for a more stable simulation while recording your animation. Save / Export Select the file format you would like to export from 'File -&gt Export' menu FBX or Alembic format is recommended if the file you create includes the animation. Animation Videos https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qP41F3EcoJk&ampt=2s https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tBvB-ppNjl8 Animation Manual Ver.12 - Animation Improvements: https://marvelousdesigner.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/12153605905049 Ver. 11 - Animation Improvements: https://marvelousdesigner.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407120017049 To find more, please search 'Animation' in our Help Center web.

Content: Objective Add and edit curve points on Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point Click the desired position of a segment to add a curve point. The Free Curve Point is added to the segment and the straight line is curved. Click and drag to add curve point and edit curvature at once. To enter Moved Distance, please right click while click-and-dragging the Curve Point (ver4.2.0). Option Description Distance Moved Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. X-Axis (ver4.2.0) Type in how much a point is moved on x-axis. This option does not appear for segments. Y-Axis (ver4.2.0) Type in how much a point is moved on Y-axis. This option does not appear for segments. Note: Moving multiple curve points at once is possible starting ver4.2.0 (ver4.2.0). The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) The Free Curve Point can be freely added and edited. The Free Curve Point can also be created by holding down the Ctrl key on the keyboard while drafting a Pattern with the Polygon tool. When a Free Curve Point is added to an AI Bezier curve, its AI Bezier curve handles disappear and the curve is reshaped based on the added Free Curve Point.
